gymnasium.definition: Athletic facility equipped for sports or physical training.

auditorium.definition: The area of a theater or concert hall where the audience sits.

art-room.definition: A dedicated classroom or studio where students create visual art under a teacher’s guidance.

music-room.definition: A room equipped or reserved for practicing, teaching, or performing music.
music-room.exampleUsage: The children practiced drums in the music room.

computer-lab.definition: Designed to recreate a computer lab through its equipment, physical arrangement, and digital resources.

meeting-room.definition: A room reserved for group meetings, often located in an office, school, hotel, or community center.

daycare.definition: Childcare during the day while parents work.

yoga-class.definition: A scheduled session in which people practice yoga postures, breathing, and relaxation.
yoga-class.exampleUsage: The community center offers a yoga class on Tuesday.

dance-class.definition: A lesson in which people learn and practice dance movements or styles.
dance-class.exampleUsage: She joined a dance class after school.

cooking-class.definition: A lesson where participants learn and practice how to prepare food.
cooking-class.exampleUsage: The cooking class focused on simple vegetable dishes.

painting-class.definition: A lesson where participants learn and practice painting techniques.
painting-class.exampleUsage: He attends a painting class on weekends.

pottery-class.definition: A lesson where participants learn to shape and decorate objects made from clay.
pottery-class.exampleUsage: The pottery class made small bowls from clay.

language-class.definition: A class uses a language other than the students’ native language for instruction, immersing them in that language.

tutoring.definition: Individual instruction helps a learner master academic skills, usually through one-on-one lessons or small-group sessions.

meditation.definition: Continuous and profound contemplation or musing on a subject or series of subjects of a deep or abstruse nature.

book-club.definition: Connected with a book club or created to help its members discuss books and share related activities.

film-night.definition: An organized evening when a film is shown to a group or community.
film-night.exampleUsage: The center held a family film night on Friday.

basketball.definition: An inflated ball used in playing basketball.

volleyball.definition: An inflated ball used in playing volleyball.

badminton.definition: A game played by hitting a shuttlecock over a net.

table-tennis.definition: A racket game similar to tennis, it is played across a table with paddles and a lightweight hollow ball.

swimming.definition: Moving through water for exercise or pleasure.

karate.definition: A traditional Japanese system of unarmed combat.

zumba.definition: A group fitness activity that combines dance movements with energetic exercise music.
zumba.exampleUsage: The Zumba class uses simple dance-based exercise routines.

aerobics.definition: Based on or using the principles of aerobics.

weight-training.definition: Exercise that uses weights or resistance to strengthen muscles.
weight-training.exampleUsage: The gym area is used for supervised weight training.

stretching.definition: Moving your body to loosen muscles and improve flexibility.

bake-sale.definition: An event where baked foods are sold, often to raise money for a group or cause.
bake-sale.exampleUsage: The club held a bake sale to raise funds for new equipment.

talent-show.definition: A public school or community event gives students a stage to perform skills such as singing, dancing, or magic. The performances entertain an audience and may be judged as a competition.

holiday-party.definition: A social gathering held to celebrate a holiday or festive season.
holiday-party.exampleUsage: The center organized a holiday party for local families.

workshop.definition: Small workplace where handcrafts or manufacturing are done.

seminar.definition: Any meeting for an exchange of ideas.

concert.definition: A performance of music by players or singers not involving theatrical staging.

farmers-market.definition: A regularly scheduled place, often outdoors, where local farmers sell fresh produce and other farm goods directly to consumers.

blood-drive.definition: An organized event where eligible volunteers donate blood for medical use.
blood-drive.exampleUsage: The community center hosted a blood drive with trained medical staff.

voting.definition: A choice that is made by counting the number of people in favor of each alternative.

bulletin-board.definition: A board where notices and student work are displayed.

water-fountain.definition: A public device that supplies drinking water.

locker.definition: A small locked compartment for a student’s belongings.

stage.definition: Any distinct time period in a sequence of events.

projector.definition: A device that displays images on a wall or screen.

whiteboard.definition: To build, examine, or clarify ideas together by writing or drawing on a whiteboard.

microphone.definition: A device that changes sound into an electrical recording or signal.

instructor.definition: A person whose occupation is teaching.

coordinator.definition: Someone whose task is to see that work goes harmoniously.

volunteer.definition: A person who freely helps without being paid.

member.definition: One of the persons who compose a social group (especially individuals who have joined and participate in a group organization).

child.definition: A young person who has not become an adult.

lifeguard.definition: An attendant employed at a beach or pool to protect swimmers from accidents.

coach.definition: A person who trains players in a sport.

receptionist.definition: A secretary whose main duty is to answer the telephone and receive visitors.

janitor.definition: A person who cleans and maintains a building.
